body:
# the contributor audit: retained surface-area measure and exact exposed-face traces

Read in full:

- `candidate d332d092619053f4`;
- `candidate 79217d237564c41f`.

Both PASS in their stated scope. The surface-area result is an ordinary
geometric ingredient; the face trace result identifies a real obstruction
to a direct lower-dimensional induction. Neither provides an OC center.

## Common area measure

Atomizing a spherical component by its cell vector integral preserves
its first moment exactly. The small cell diameter makes that vector
nonzero and bounds its norm between (1-delta^2/2) times the cell mass
and the cell mass. The atom's direction stays within O(delta) of the
cell. This gives direct weak convergence while retaining a shared
component in both full approximate measures. No continuity of taking
the wedge of two independently convergent measures is asserted.

The full approximations have exact equilibrium. A finite-net argument
gives uniform convergence of their absolute first projections, whose
limit has a strictly positive minimum. Hence the approximations satisfy
the nonconcentration hypothesis of the classical Minkowski theorem.
That theorem applies to the FULL measures, not to the common component,
which need not itself be balanced or be an area measure.

The inverse compactness proof is correct. Cauchy's projection formula
bounds all (d-1)-projection volumes above and below. A translated John
ellipsoid with semiaxes a_i, product p, then has every p/a_i bounded
above and below. Their product is p^(d-1), so all semiaxes are uniformly
bounded above and away from zero. Blaschke compactness thus supplies
full-dimensional limits. Weak area-measure continuity and Minkowski
uniqueness identify these with translates of the original bodies.
Translations have no effect on the required area inequalities.

At a retained common atom, both polytopes have actual parallel facets
of at least its mass. The exposed face of the Minkowski mean is their
Minkowski mean. Ordinary (d-1)-dimensional Brunn--Minkowski gives the
same lower bound on its facet area. Passing this measure domination
against nonnegative continuous tests is legitimate. The proof covers
atoms, singular continuous parts, and arbitrary mixtures without
smoothing away shared measure.

The finite weighted extension uses the common component only once,
with the specified constant coefficients, and atomizes each positive
residual separately. Equilibrium and simultaneous compactness remain
valid. Zero coefficients and lower-dimensional exposed faces do not
invalidate Brunn--Minkowski. The further density-root statement follows
by restricting the common reference measure to disjoint value bins of
its Radon--Nikodym densities, applying the constant-coefficient theorem
on each bin, restricting its conclusion back to that bin, and taking
the mesh to zero. This avoids any unproved variable-coefficient use
of the atomic construction.

## Exposed face and inward collar

The entire contact face has a lattice-complete base because integer
convex combinations of its actual points stay on its supporting plane.
The same is true for positive (d-1)-measure fibers by combining relative
interior balls. Continuous rotation and the affine shear subtracting
the support height preserve each integer base and each fiber's tangent
Hausdorff measure. The rational base direction space has a saturated
lattice, so unimodular rank reduction is legitimate. Relative interior
of the reduced face hull follows from independent bases and positive
tangent balls. The zero-dimensional exception is explicitly separated.

At inward distance t the cap margin is exactly its face margin minus
c t, with c the normal component of its continuous cap normal. Proper
tangent zero sets are area-null, while an identically zero face margin
has inward bit1 precisely when c<=0. Slice Hausdorff convergence and
bounded tangent support justify dominated convergence for ANY function
of finitely many cap bits. Zero-area contact fibers have collar mass
o(epsilon); noncontact fibers have a fixed positive gap. These facts
justify the finite sum and the closed-boundary correction exactly.

The example with three unit rectangle fibers checks directly: two
caps have identical closed traces on the top face but normalized inward
collar masses1 and2. Every face point also lies in the original exterior
supporting cap of zero d-volume, so its original depth is zero. Thus
an inductive face center is not a center for the original measure.
The quoted canonical triangle facet profile has mean4/9 and convex
test optimum4/9, not1/2; the chord-subtraction proof has the correct
signs. These are substantive barriers to an automatic dimension drop,
not an OC counterexample.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
